english.title: Trespass on a protected site
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), as a trespasser, entered or were on a protected site which was a

(A)_[nuclear site,]_
(B)_[designated site,]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 128 of the Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 128 of the Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005 (as amended by section 12 of Terrorism Act 2006) provides definitions in relation to protected and nuclear sites, 'designated' was substituted by 'protected', i.e. 'nuclear' OR 'designated' site. This amendment came into force on 13th April 2006.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Attorney General, see section 128(6) of the Act.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Until the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the penalty will be - Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
